This Fully Bespoke Camper Van Is a Luxurious Mobile Home With Plenty of Ingenious Features
20 photos
Photo: Vanboerse/ YouTube screenshot
Most travelers and aspiring vanlifers are looking for a personalized experience, so a custom camper van conversion tailored specifically to their needs and tastes is the way to go. For many customers, this means a unique layout, hand-picked finishes, and special features meant to make their life on the road easier and more pleasant.
Camper Schmiede, a premium camper van manufacturer based in Germany’s Lower Rhine region, takes this approach to heart, offering their customers the opportunity to create true dream campers. Instead of standard layouts and fixed features, the company works closely with each client to develop unique conversions around their specific requirements.
With a focus on high-quality materials, first-class craftsmanship, and attention to detail, the team builds rigs that feel clearly different from the mass-produced ones. The camper van featured here is one of Camper Schmiede’s latest creations, a fully bespoke MAN TGE conversion with an ingenious bathroom, a home cinema system, and an elevator bed.
Built on a brand-new MAN TGE equipped with a 177-hp engine and an eight-speed automatic transmission, this camper van measures 6.8 meters (22.3 feet) long and 2.8 meters (9.2 feet) tall, providing just enough interior space to create a comfortable mobile habitat.
Photo: Vanboerse/ YouTube screenshot Finished in Indium Gray Metallic, its exterior combines ruggedness with elegance. The team adorned it with several customer-requested features, such as a front light bar and rugged rear-mounted carriers from Overland Equipment, providing space for storage boxes, a spare tire, and additional gear. On top of the van, there is a large roof rack with a rooftop terrace and walkable solar panels.
Built using a lightweight aluminum honeycomb system, the roof terrace is a great addition for outdoor lovers, offering an additional space to hang out. A full-length awning is also installed on the side, providing a shade area at camp. As such, owners have two options for enjoying the outdoors: relax next to the camper or head up to the roof with a cup of coffee and a different view of their surroundings.
Designed for anything from weekend escapes to full-time van living , the interior is warm and functional, with custom-made furniture and a layout designed to ensure everyday comfort. Camper Schmiede efficiently used the available space, squeezing in a generous lounge, a fully equipped kitchen, an ingenious bathroom/closet system, and a proper bed that descends from the ceiling.
Photo: Vanboerse/ YouTube screenshot One of the highlights inside this custom van is the inventive rotating closet and shower system that allows for flexible space utilization. On the outside, the 2-in-1 system features regular doors revealing storage, but another handle reveals this is a rotating module where the closets are built directly in the path of the wet bath door. When you open the bathroom door to use the shower, the closet effectively slides out of the wet bath, revealing a full-height, isolated shower stall.
The bathroom itself includes a water-saving recirculating shower that captures, filters, sterilizes, and reuses shower water in a closed loop, making it possible to enjoy luxurious hot showers off-grid. A vanity counter with a small sink and a Clesana X1 portable, heat-sealing toilet tucked away in a dedicated compartment are also included.
There is a second, larger wardrobe next to the bathroom, providing more space for clothes and personal belongings, as well as a narrow heated compartment with an air vent, designed to dry damp clothes or equipment.
Photo: Vanboerse/ YouTube screenshot Like in most camper conversions , the kitchen stretches along one side of the van and features custom cabinetry in dark gray and a wood-toned solid countertop. In terms of cooking equipment, the customer opted for an undermount sink with a cutting board insert, an integrated cooktop, an oven, and a refrigerator.
What makes this van different from other conversions is that both the cooktop and the oven run on diesel, as does the integrated hydronic underfloor heating system. And since diesel is the primary energy source, the owner won’t have to carry gas cylinders or rely fully on battery energy for cooking and heating.
The cabinetry and countertop run the entire length of the van, with an angular shape in the lounge area to facilitate easy circulation. It gradually narrows toward the rear and then transforms into a nice shelving unit that completes the lounge area.
Photo: Vanboerse/ YouTube screenshot Speaking of the lounge, instead of two opposing benches, the client opted for a large L-shaped built-in sofa with comfortable seating for four. It is accompanied by an adjustable table for dining/working functionality, while a projector and screen turn the space into a home theater. The projector attaches magnetically to the underside of the elevator bed, so you can easily remove it if you want to use it outside, for instance.
When it’s time for sleep, the bed drops down from the ceiling at the push of a button. It’s a full-fledged longitudinal bed measuring 2 by 1.45 meters (6.6 by 4.8 feet) and comes with a Gisamed premium folding mattress. There is also a skylight from Outbound above the bed for stargazing.
Up front in the driver’s cabin, Camper Schmiede swapped out the original driver and passenger seats for custom Scheel-Mann seats for an extra level of comfort. They both swivel to face the living space and offer extra seating. Above the cab, an enclosed compartment offers a generous amount of storage space, while a narrow shelf behind the driver’s seat could easily be used as a nice space to work on your laptop, though the rear lounge would be much more comfortable for remote work.
Photo: Vanboerse/ YouTube screenshot Designed for self-sufficient travel, this MAN GTE camper van is equipped with 350 watts of solar panels on the roof and a Victron electrical system to manage the onboard power. Both the fresh-water and gray-water tanks are mounted underneath the vehicle, freeing up valuable interior storage space. Each tank holds approximately 150 liters (40 gallons), which the builder says would be enough for about a week, with the recirculating shower really boosting the “self-sufficiency” factor.
This particular van conversion is not equipped with one, but Camper Schmiede offers an optional feature called the Soul Floater. It’s an ergonomic, fold-out lounger that attaches to the rear of the vehicle and accommodates two adults, with a maximum load capacity of 200 kg (441 lbs).
Since this is a fully custom build , no pricing information is available, but Camper Schmiede’s conversions typically hover around the €269,000 mark, which is approximately $299,500 at the current exchange rate.

source_document.body:
China's Test Spacecraft 3 spaceplane, taken May 28, 2024 by Vantor's WorldView-3 satellite (Image credit: Vantor)
WASHINGTON — A new report by the Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) finds that China has tripled its fleet of intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) satellites since 2018 and continues to expand capabilities to detect, track and target US and allied forces on the ground and at sea.
“China employs a robust space-based ISR capability designed to enhance its worldwide situational awareness and enable long-range strikes,” including electro-optical (EO) and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery satellites and others that provide electronic and signals intelligence data, according to the DIA’s 2026 Challenges to Space Security report, released Monday.
The report says China’s ISR satellite network can help the PLA monitor and target US and allied forces worldwide, particularly across the Indo-Pacific — including the Korean Peninsula, Taiwan, the Philippines, the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea.
The DIA report echoes concerns from US Space Force and Space Command about the PLA’s growing ability to build “kill chains” to target US joint forces abroad and at home.
Clayton Swope, deputy director of the Center for Strategic and International Studies’ Aerospace Security Project, said China is investing heavily in space-based sensors to monitor Earth and identify, track and target objects in the Indo-Pacific.
“A concern on the minds of US and allied decision makers should be how PLA sensor webs could erode US advantages derived from stealth in the air and undersea domains. Will we be able to operate undetected in the air and undersea domains in the future?” he told Breaking Defense.
Echoing a July 2026 Space Force fact sheet on space threats, the DIA report states that China had more than 510 ISR satellites in orbit as of July. Unlike the Space Force document, however, the DIA report acknowledges that its count includes satellites owned by both the People’s Republic of China and Chinese commercial firms.
“While many of these ISR satellites are ostensibly affiliated with commercial and civil missions, the dual-use nature of their capabilities and possibly the Chinese military-civil fusion policies means the data or imagery they collect can be used by the PLA,” the report says.
The DIA also says Chinese commercial firms are supplying imagery “to state actors banned by Western providers for supporting weapons proliferation.”
China’s ISR fleet continues to expand and improve technologically, the DIA report stresses, particularly through Beijing’s growing constellation of satellites in low Earth orbit.
However, American Enterprise Institute’s (AEI) Senior Fellow Todd Harrison said the DIA’s data is unclear about which satellites are included in its count and also lacks important context.
He told Breaking Defense that China’s operational surveillance and weather satellite fleet has grown from 141 in 2018 to 541 today, while its surveillance-only fleet has increased from 124 to 453. “What those numbers don’t tell you is that the slope of the curve has leveled off in recent years — the number of satellites is not increasing as fast,” Harrison said.
Meanwhile, the US has 643 operational surveillance and weather satellites — up from 298 in 2018 — and is expanding its ISR fleet faster than China, he said.
The following chart, created for Breaking Defense from AEI’s Space Data Navigator , shows that trend.
The DIA report is the third in a series of unclassified reports examining US concerns about adversary advancements in military space, with the first version published in 2019.
The new report covers space threats emanating from China, Russia and “emerging” space powers.
It also looks at developments expected to exacerbate future challenges to US interests in space. Among those listed in the 2026 report: reusable space systems, such as rockets and spaceplanes; increasing use of artificial intelligence; orbital congestion; the collision risk posed by the many non-maneuverable spacecraft that will remain on orbit long after becoming inoperable; and the growing interest in satellites stationed in very low Earth orbit.
Intriguingly, the report includes what appears to be the first public image of China’s reusable spaceplane , most recently launched in February . The spaceplane is widely believed to be modeled after the US X-37B. Victoria Samson, chief director of space security and stability at the Secure World Foundation, said the image appears to support that assessment.
“It looks a lot like the X-37B!” she told Breaking Defense.
The DIA concludes by predicting that space will become increasingly congested and competitive as capabilities advance and more countries expand their presence in the domain.
“The increase of Chinese, Russian, Iranian, and North Korean counterspace capabilities, rapid growth in the number of space objects, and the proliferation of requirements for space-enabled services will all complicate operations in space in the coming decade,” the report adds.

2026 SEMA Show • Honda Racing Releases Its First-Ever In-House Made Parts for the Civic Type R and Integra Type S
World's Only Targa Top Barracuda Was Made in 1964 as a Styling Exercise, It's Ridiculously Cheap Now
96 photos
Photo: Bring A Trailer/PatsRareRides
Plymouth is long gone, but its legacy will live for as long as there will be cars and car nuts. The low-cost ChryCo division has the often-overlooked merit of debuting the pony car - ironically called after the Ford Mustang that succeeded the Barracuda by two weeks in April 1964. It also has the merit of creating the first American car with a Targa Top (not to be confused with T-tops): the 1964 Plymouth Barracuda Landau. The only one ever made. This one.
Typically, old cars depreciate in value after a while, right around the time they become “old cars” for the first time. No, I didn’t just shoot myself in the foot with a one-bore grammar-filled slug. Old cars have different degrees of “old.” They’re “just old cars” at first (that no one wants), then they’re “old cars” that are cool, but not really worth much, and then they’re “old cars” worth either their scrap value, or their weight in gold.
Some of those old cars make spectacular comebacks. Anyone care to explain the Hemicuda convertible and their seven-figure sale prices? I'll wait. But not all super-rare and roofless Barracudas are worth millions. This one seen in the gallery - and in the video attached below - isn't even on the “good deal” side of four figures (from a seller’s standpoint), despite being the only one ever made.
That shocking affordability has followed this one-off “corporate design study” across multiple auction blocks. According to the Hagerty Price Guide, the prototype appeared at the RM Sotheby's Auburn Fall auction in September 2010, where it went unsold at a $24,000 high bid. After 16 years, on September 26, 2026, it crossed the Mecum Nashville block for just $21,000 (buyer paid $23,100).
Photo: Bring A Trailer/PatsRareRides As of now, it has a high bid of $22,500 on Bring A Trailer (with four days left), where it will go without reserve. The selling dealer explained the no-reserve listing decision: "It was selling at the end of the auction on Saturday. [September 26]. Late entry to the auction with no marketing. The seats were empty. Empty as in 95% of the crowd gone. When it sold even I couldn’t believe it. IMO BaT is the best platform to sell a unique prototype like this. That is why I chose to sell it without reserve."
Built on the final Thursday of 1964 production, this Valiant-based fastback was immediately requisitioned by Chrysler stylists, who removed the main steel roof panel to test an open-air Landau concept while keeping the arched rear roof hoop – and its signature back window (the largest single piece of glass fitted to a production passenger car).
Finished from the factory in code A Gold and repainted under prior ownership, the exterior features a split grille, front vent windows, V8 fender badges, a deck-lid Valiant emblem, reverse lights, and wraparound chrome bumpers. It rides on 13-inch steel wheels with styled covers and National Horizon polyester whitewalls, showing chipped paint and pitted brightwork.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/PatsRareRides Under the hood sits a 273-cubic-inch LA V8 fed by a Carter two-barrel carburetor, factory rated at 180 horsepower at 4,200 rpm and 260 lb-ft of torque at 1,600 rpm. Power reaches the rear wheels through a push-button TorqueFlite 3-speed automatic transmission, while power-assisted 4-wheel drum brakes boast a new master cylinder.
Inside, gold vinyl covers the worn front bucket seats and fold-down rear bench alongside a Valiant Transaudio AM radio.
A three-spoke steering wheel fronts a 110-mph speedometer and an odometer showing 52,446 miles, (15 miles added by the seller in their sole month of ownership). The white fabric roof panel is damaged and fits poorly, prompting Bring a Trailer commenters to joke about spending beer tokens fabricating a weather-tight top that stays attached at speed. Curiously, the top seemed to be holding on quite well back when the car was photographed for the Mecum listing. Maybe the seller has more details.
Photo: Mecum Sharp-eyed readers also spotted smoothed rear quarter-to-valance seams, crumbling seat foam, and an open gap behind the door glass.
Mopar experts in the comments also diagnosed the car's electrical and suspension quirks. The two non-working gauges for gas and coolant temperature likely stem from a failed voltage limiter, a common issue that is the culprit when both gauges fail. Meanwhile, the hunched stance with the lowered front is probably due to the torsion bar setting.
It should be a straightforward and fairly simple fix: crank the torsion bars to factory specs and this Barracuda will look great again. Speaking of looks, let’s set things straight about the body style. This Barracuda Landau is a Targa top, not a T-top and not a convertible. A Targa top uses a full-width removable panel ahead of a fixed roll bar bridging the B-pillars while retaining the rear glass.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/PatsRareRides Before Porsche trademarked the Targa name after Sicily's Targa Florio race for its 1966-model 911 amid fears of a federal convertible ban, Giovanni Michelotti pioneered the layout on the 1957 Fiat 1200 Wonderful.
Michelotti reprised that idea on the 1961 Triumph TR4, followed by the 1964 Saab Catherina, this 1964 Barracuda, the 1965 Toyota Sports 800, the 1971 Fiat X1/9, Griffith's 1978 Celica Sunchaser and 1981 AMC Eagle Sundancer, and every Corvette coupe since 1984. Conversely, T-tops use split panels divided by a fixed center bar running lengthwise from the windshield to the rear.
This T-tops arrangement was invented by Gordon Buehrig on the airplane-inspired 1948 TASCO prototype (The American Sportscar Company), and patented in 1951.
Photo: Mecum After lying dormant for 20 years, T-tops ignited a craze when General Motors introduced them on the 1968 Corvette, prompting a patent lawsuit from Buehrig. Touted as taking 10 seconds to lift off, T-top Corvettes outsold roadsters and killed the convertible after 1975 until 1986. Throughout the 1970s, T-tops spread across Detroit on the 1975 Hurst/Olds, 1976 Trans Am, 1978 Camaro, Buick Regal, Chrysler Cordoba, Dodge Magnum, Ford Thunderbird, and Mustang.
Despite testing this open-roof Landau in 1964, Plymouth never built a first-generation drop-top, waiting until the 1967 redesign to launch the first factory Barracuda convertible, totaling 4,228 units. All first-gen pony Mopars remained fixed-roof fastbacks.
Following its April 1, 1964 debut, Plymouth produced 23,443 units before the regular 1965 production year began, totaling 64,596 cars during the actual 1965 model year, offering versatile Slant-Six and small-block V8 engine choices.
Photo: Bring A Trailer/PatsRareRides After dropping 1964's 101-horsepower 170-cubic-inch Slant-6, the 1965 lineup featured a 145-horsepower 225-cubic-inch Slant-Six, the 180-horsepower 273-cubic-inch two-barrel V8, and a 235-horsepower 273-cubic-inch four-barrel Commando V8.
Transmission choices included a column-shifted 3-speed manual, a floor-shifted 4-speed manual, or the 3-speed TorqueFlite automatic. With a V8-powered Barracuda carrying a base price of $2,493 in 1964 and $2,571 in 1965, how much do you think a factory Targa-top Barracuda would have cost back then?

2026 SEMA Show • Mitsubishi Returns to Las Vegas With the Fresh 2028 Outlander Diamond Trail Edition
New Hot Wheels Elite 64 Mercedes-AMG ONE Is Just Around the Corner
12 photos
Photo: Mattel Creations
I am sometimes shocked at how quickly Mattel will come out with a 1/64th-scale version of a car that just debuted on the international stage. It can take up to a year in some cases, and I guess it all depends on the deals that go on behind the scenes. It’s not always smooth sailing, though.
Take for instance the Ferrari situation. The diecast manufacturer had lost the license over a decade ago, and Hot Wheels fans had no other choice but to get their tiny prancing ponies from other companies. That problem is being dealt with right now, ever since Mattel and Ferrari signed a new agreement circa 2024.
I know the Heritage Set showed up as a Red Line Club special release in 2025, but think of the development process and time needed to get that result. Anyway, I’m not here to talk about Hot Wheels Ferraris, as Mercedes-AMG is the star of the show here. Seeing this brand-new casting reminds me I just missed purchasing the '89 Mercedes-Benz 560 SEC AMG from my local dealer.
And something tells me that its first-ever Premium variation is just as desirable as the Elite 64 collectible in today’s story. And that also brings me back to what I was saying earlier: this car has been around since 2022! We’ve had to wait four years for a Hot Wheels version of it, and I can think of a few reasons why it hasn’t happened so far.
The licensing costs might have been too high for the deal to make sense, or maybe the team in El Segundo just didn’t know which series this casting would best fit in. Elite 64 launched in 2023, but it was a rather slow start with only six items in one year. Anyway, it’s just around the corner now, and I must say I am slightly disappointed it doesn’t feature the opening gullwing doors like the real thing.
I realize that could have placed it in RLC-exclusive territory, where it would have wound up costing $35 or more. Resellers in my area are already asking a bit more than that as they’re taking advantage of the shipping restrictions, so there’s that. The AMG One is the third Mercedes collectible in Elite 64 this year, after the 300 SL and the G 63 AMG 6×6.
I pre-ordered the latter a while ago and I’m not sure what happened to it. We all know the AMG One won’t be nearly as desirable as the upcoming hauler that several creators have been teasing recently. That one is bound to sell out within the first 60 seconds, while the Mercedes hypercar might even become a virtual peg-warmer (at least for a few weeks).
I’m not convinced this series will survive beyond 2027, but I also don’t have any sort of access to any numbers on how it’s going. I don’t plan on buying this collectible, but you can give it a try on the 29th of October , 2026 at 9 AM PT. I have to admit the presentation photos are pretty cool, though!

Waymo service areas after the expansion. Maps: Waymo
Waymo is growing its driverless service area by nearly 250 square miles over the next week, spread across Los Angeles, Nashville, Orlando, San Diego, and the San Francisco Bay Area.
That’s about as big as Tesla’s entire Houston Robotaxi geofence after this week’s expansion, and Waymo is adding it in cities where it already runs with nobody in the driver’s seat.
Where Waymo is expanding
The company announced the expansion in a short post on its blog today. Here’s what changes in each market, with Waymo’s updated service area maps:
Los Angeles
Service now runs down the coast into the South Bay, through Manhattan Beach and Redondo Beach to Torrance.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Waymo’s Los Angeles service area after the expansion (Image: Waymo)
Nashville
The zone pushes further south, and riders can now get to the zoo.
Waymo’s Nashville service area after the expansion (Image: Waymo)
Orlando
Coverage on the east side nearly doubles, and there’s more service downtown.
Waymo’s Orlando service area after the expansion (Image: Waymo)
San Diego
The service area now stretches north to La Jolla, taking in University City and Clairemont along the way.
Waymo’s San Diego service area after the expansion (Image: Waymo)
San Francisco Bay Area
Waymo is pushing further into the South Bay, including a connection to BART at Berryessa station in San Jose. The service area now runs from San Francisco down the Peninsula to San Jose and Campbell.
Waymo’s San Francisco Bay Area service area after the expansion (Image: Waymo)
Waymo didn’t break out square mileage by city, and it didn’t say how many vehicles it’s adding to cover the new ground. The updated maps are already in the Waymo app.
Some of these markets are very young. Waymo opened Nashville to public riders in April with a zone of about 60 square miles covering downtown, Midtown, Music Row, and East Nashville. San Diego only went public on September 1, with roughly 50 square miles between the beach and I-15 that barely crossed north of I-8. So getting to La Jolla less than two months later is a big jump.
The gap keeps growing
In May, Waymo pushed its coverage past 1,400 square miles across 11 cities, which is bigger than the state of Rhode Island. Since then, it went driverless in Las Vegas , launched San Diego, and now says it operates in 15 US metros with more than 500,000 paid rides per week. It’s even mapping Toronto for a 2028 launch .
Tesla is also drawing bigger maps. After launching Robotaxi in Dallas and Houston with tiny geofences in April, it stretched Houston to about 254 square miles this week, according to Robotaxi Tracker. But the tracker counts 34 vehicles in Houston.
And on the metric that reflects actual use, it’s not close. Waymo logged 3.9 million rider-only miles per week in Q2 2026, while Tesla’s driverless fleet did 558,000 miles in its latest reported week, mostly in Austin. That’s about 7x, and it comes on the same day Elon Musk claimed the robotaxi race against Waymo “was never a real contest.”
Electrek’s Take
I like this. Good progress. But I’ll be truly impressed when the Bay Area service area extends south into LA, expands north, and the same happens in San Diego.
It’s going to happen. Waymo is already dabbling with highway operations in California. I can see them linking all those service areas within the next 2 years. Maybe even by the end of next year if all goes well.

Mexican trucking organizations reached an agreement with federal officials Tuesday to begin negotiations aimed at resolving a nationwide strike that disrupted highways across 19 states,
The agreement between Mexico’s Interior Ministry (Segob) and trucking groups, including the National Chamber of Freight Transport (CANACAR), calls for four high-level working sessions addressing highway security, infrastructure, tax incentives, regulations and other issues affecting the country’s freight transportation industry.
Truckers launched nationwide demonstrations on Monday, demanding government action against cargo theft , highway robberies with violence , extortion and rising operating costs.
The agreement arises after trade and freight transportation officials raised concerns about freight transportation and supply chain delays, according to reporting by La Jornada , T21 and Revista Transportes y Turismo .
Mexico’s Interior Ministry reported demonstrations at 38 locations across 19 states Monday morning, involving 691 vehicles and 858 participants. The protests included truck convoys, roadside gatherings and highway blockades.
CANACAR disputed the government’s assessment of the demonstrations, saying the protest movement extended across all 32 Mexican states.
Augusto Ramos Melo, president of CANACAR, met Tuesday with Interior Ministry officials alongside Carlos García Álvarez, president of the Honorable Mexican Alliance of Transport Organizations (HAMOTAC), and Lauro Rincón Hernández, president of the Mexican-American Federation of Transporters (FEMATRAC).
Following the meeting, Ramos Melo announced that four negotiating sessions would be established to address the industry’s demands.
However, the organizations had not confirmed that all demonstrations had ended.
Earlier Tuesday, CANACAR and other trucking organizations had called on participants to continue peaceful demonstrations at strategic highway locations while negotiations were being arranged.
The protests have highlighted longstanding concerns among Mexican trucking companies over cargo theft, violence against truck drivers, extortion and the costs of operating commercial vehicles.
Why it matters: Mexico’s nationwide trucking protests underscore the vulnerability of freight corridors supporting U.S.-Mexico trade, while the new negotiations could determine whether carriers face additional disruptions in the coming days.

Microsoft OCP 2026 - Maia 300 Node-6
At OCP 2026, I was fortunate to share an Uber ride from the hotel to the convention center with Microsoft’s project manager for the Maia 300, the company’s new in-house AI acceleration platform. I promised that we would cover it, so it is time, because it is a neat platform. OCP Summit 2026 was much larger than it has been, but keeping with tradition, Microsoft had an awesome booth.
Microsoft Maia 300 Shown at OCP 2026
A few weeks before OCP 2026, at Hot Chips 2026, Microsoft did a deep-dive on the Maia 200 . For OCP, it showed the next-generation chip, the Maia 300. This has eight HBM4 stacks for 288GB of memory and 18TB/s of memory bandwidth, and 3.2TB/s of scale-up bidirectional bandwidth.
Microsoft Maia 300 Node Key Specs Large
Microsoft says that it fits 96 Maia’s into a rack and roughly 12K in the scale-up domain. Instead of just bringing a chip to the show, they brought an entire 4-accelerator node, which is what makes OCP awesome.
Microsoft OCP 2026 – Maia 300 Node-4
Just to give folks a look, here is the overhead view of the node from a stock photo.
Microsoft Maia 300 Node Overhead Stock Large
One thing you can clearly see is that the 950W TDP accelerators are covered by a liquid-cooled cold plate.
Microsoft OCP 2026 – Maia 300 Node-7
You can also see what look like MCIO x16 connectors on the board, but more interestingly, there are many cabled connections. Our best guess is that these are UltraPass connectors that help scale within the node.
Microsoft OCP 2026 – Maia 300 Node-6
Microsoft has a pretty neat PCIe topology and extensive fabric connectivity throughout the chassis.
Microsoft OCP 2026 – Maia 300 Node-9
Another item we noticed is that this is not an all-liquid-cooled design. The CPU, SSDs, OCP NIC 3.0 devices, and many components around the AI accelerators are cooled by a massive fan partition that spans the chassis.
Microsoft OCP 2026 – Maia 300 Node-3
At the rear, it connects to busbar power, blind mate liquid cooling, and its scale-up network. One thing is very noticeable here. Whereas NVIDIA is designing its Vera Rubin NVL72 nodes and infrastructure to use fewer cables, Microsoft is all-in on cables, as even each accelerator is on its own PCB with multiple cables, and there are many PCBs in this system.
Microsoft OCP 2026 – Maia 300 Node-1
You may have also noticed that this is more like a 1.5x standard OU width, but not quite the double-wide width of the AMD Helios . When you are customizing this much inside the server, from designing the ASICs, perhaps customizing the racks as well is not a big deal.
Final Words
Microsoft makes some really cool stuff, and this is not an exception. You may have seen the Massive Microsoft Azure HBv4 AMD EPYC Genoa Heatsink years ago, where even the custom-designed heatsinks are just cool. Of course, the components have well over 4kW TDP, and a rack has 24 of these trays, so I know STH readers love seeing new AI accelerators with lots of bandwidth.
As an aside here, when I saw the 288GB HBM4 and 950W specs, a part of me wondered what would happen if there was ever a way to have something like the DGX Station (e.g., this Gigabyte or this MSI, and the Supermicro review will be next week) with these accelerators. Even though these are six-figure tower systems, from what I have heard, demand is crazy. That would probably take Microsoft deciding it wanted to build a developer ecosystem and start selling Maia, but it would be interesting, especially if it hit a lower price point.

BYD updated its lowest-priced electric car, the Seagull, which starts at around $10,000 in China, with a few extras, including a high-speed tire blowout system that stabilizes the vehicle at nearly 90 mph.
BYD’s new Seagull EV is bigger and more advanced
If the $10,000 price tag wasn’t enough, BYD is giving buyers even more reason to check out its entry-level electric hatch.
The Seagull is among BYD’s most popular vehicles, sold as the Dolphin Surf in Europe and the UK and as the Dolphin Mini in other global markets.
BYD launched the second-generation Seagull EV last week, starting at just 62,900 yuan, or about $9,500. That’s including BYD’s limited-time Super Trade-In incentive.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Regular prices start at 65,900 yuan ($9,900), which is still less than its predecessor. The first-generation Seagull EV started at 69,900 yuan ($10,500) without incentives, making it BYD’s most affordable purely electric vehicle in China.
For its second generation, the Seagull is bigger, more advanced, and adds a bit more luxury to the entry-level segment.
The new BYD Seagull is 4,205 mm long, 1,810 mm wide, and 1,570 mm high, with a 2,650 mm wheelbase. That’s 425 mm longer and has a 150 mm longer wheelbase than the previous model.
Thanks to the added space, BYD’s electric hatch now offers room for five passengers, up from four seats that the first-gen Seagull had.
BYD added several new features with its latest tech, including a bigger 15.6″ infotainment screen with its DiLink 150 smart cockpit system and a “140 km/h high-speed tire blowout stability system” as standard.
To showcase how the tire blowout system works, BYD put the updated electric hatch to the test at full speed.
BYD second-generation Seagull EV survives 140 km/h high-speed tire blowout (Source: Zhang Zhuo)
BYD’s general manager of the Ocean Series, Zhang Zhuo, shared a video of the second-generation Seagull EV handling the blowout at 140 km/h, or about 87 mph, like it’s nothing.
The high-speed tire-blowout system lets the Seagull stay in its lane until it comes to a complete stop. Pretty impressive for an entry-level vehicle.
As you can see in the video, the new version also has an available roof-mounted LiDAR. Buyers can upgrade to the optional DiPilot 300 system with BYD’s God’s Eye intelligent driving assistance. The ADAS system provides features like City Navigation on Autopilot (CNOA) and smart parking.
BYD second-generation Seagull EV interior (Source: BYD)
BYD added a few premium extras, including heating, ventilation, and a massage function to the front seats, plus ambient lighting, smart storage options, and a 50W wireless phone charger.
The new Seagull uses BYD’s Blade Batteries 2.0 and Flash Charging Technology. As such, the battery can charge from 10% to 70% in five minutes. A full recharge, or 10% to 97%, takes just nine minutes. Even in temperatures as low as -30°C, it takes 12 minutes to charge from 20% to 97%.
BYD second-generation Seagull EV (Source: Zhang Zhuo)
It’s available with two LFP battery packs: 30.1 kWh and 39.2 kWh, providing CLTC ranges of 320 km (199 miles) and 420 km (261 miles), respectively.
To improve the ride quality and handling, BYD upgraded the rear suspension to a multi-link independent system.
BYD second-generation Seagull EV (Source: Zhang Zhuo)
The second-gen Seagull also switches to front-wheel-drive (FWD) with a more powerful 85 kW (114 hp) or 95 kW (127 hp) electric motor, up from the 55 kW (75 hp) that its predecessor offered.
BYD’s new Seagull is available in five variants, priced from 65,900 yuan to 99,900 yuan ($9,900 to $15,000), without a trade-in.
After launching the second-gen Seagull in China, BYD is expected to introduce the updated version overseas. It will likely be the second-generation Dolphin Surf and Dolphin Mini.

Volkswagen’s latest recall now extends to Audi, affecting more than 9,000 Q4 E-Tron and Q4 Sportback E-Tron vehicles. And just like with the ID.4, owners are being told to limit charging to 80% of the battery’s capacity.
Volkswagen EV recall extends to Audi
Earlier this month, Volkswagen issued a recall impacting 22,524 ID.4 electric SUVs, model years 2023 to 2026.
The recall is due to the risk of thermal propagation, or a battery fire, under certain conditions when charged to over 80% of its limit.
Volkswagen said in a safety recall report with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) that “certain charging profiles combined with a state of charge over 80% may trigger thermal propagation.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
While the root cause is unknown, Volkswagen urged owners to limit charging to 80%. Owners of affected vehicles received an email saying VW “intends to apply a temporary vehicle setting that limits charging to 80%,” unless they opted out by October 21.
In the letter sent to the NHTSA on October 23, Volkswagen Group of America said it was issuing a recall affecting 9,048 Audi Q4 E-Tron and Q4 Sportback E-Tron vehicles model years 2024 to 2025.
The safety recall follows Audi’s Product Safety Committee being informed of battery thermal events involving other Volkswagen Group EVs that use the same batteries as the Audi Q4 E-Tron.
Audi Q4 E-Tron (Source: Audi)
Following an internal investigation, Audi found the same battery and production characteristics as the impacted VW Group vehicles. Audi said the majority of these were produced for the North American market.
Audi is not aware of any claims, crashes, fires, injuries, or deaths associated with the Q4 E-Tron’s battery issue.
The root cause has yet to be determined, and until a remedy is available, Audi is advising owners to limit charging to 80%.
Audi Q4 E-Tron (Source: Audi)
Owners can take their vehicles to an authorized Audi dealer, where the dealer will run a diagnostic check on the battery. If needed, the dealer will impose a temporary state-of-charge limit to 80%.
Audi expects to mail out interim letters notifying owners of the safety risks on December 18, 2026. Additional letters will send additional letters once a remedy is available.
Owners can contact Audi’s customer service at 1-800-253-2834 with questions or concerns. Audi’s recall number is 93SK. You can also contact the NHTSA Hotline at 1-888-327-4236 or visit nhtsa.gov for more information. The NHTSA campaign number is 26V698.
Volkswagen’s battery recall doesn’t just affect electric vehicles in the US. Last week, Volkswagen Group issued three separate recalls with the German Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA), affecting 72,668 EVs worldwide, including 9,881 in Germany.
The recall affects certain batches of the ID. Buzz, ID.3, ID.4, and ID.7 models produced between 2022 and 2025, as well as Cupra Born models from 2022 to 2024.

Jaison Drops Poki Mini Bike With One-Touch and Customizable Wheelie Mode – Has a $1,800 Price Tag
24 photos
Photo: Jaison Bike
The electric mini bike industry has really been taking off lately, and in the wave of rides we can find the fresh Poki from Jaison. It’s not an e-bike, but rather, a full-blown mini bike which really has the proper feeling to it. Time to take a look at what's in store here.
Jaison Bike is one of those teams that caught the electrification wave and in it, grew to sell their mobility solutions worldwide. Ive seen them on the streets of the US and as far as Europe. Well, they just dropped word of the newest addition to their family: the Poki.
Now, what makes this one so special is that Jaison broke away from the traditional e-bikes that we’re used to from them, and instead, brings to life a pedal-less machine that relies on nothing other than throttle to move around. Just kick back and enjoy the ride, literally. To do that, there are a few systems to do so, and not just throttle; we’ll get to all that.
Photo: Jaison Bike First off, we have ourselves the overall design of the Poki, completed from what I can only guess is steel because this thing weighs 137.5 lbs (62.3 kg). Sure, the motor and battery are to blame for the heavy weight, but that only goes so far, so I have my money on steel tubes for the rest of the weight.
Speaking of the battery and motor, at its core, the Poki is built upon a 60 V ecosystem, granting us access to some rather punchy acceleration. Couple that with a motor that peaks at a whopping 6,720 W, or a bit over 9 hp, so yes, I can see the minibike vibes for sure.
According to Jaison’s website, the 60 V and 9 hp amount to a top speed of as much as 50 mph (80 kph), although some riders have mentioned that they’ve been able to go beyond that number. A 60 V and 80 A controller is there managing all the flow of juice. A “tiny menace” indeed.
Photo: Jaison Bike Why so much spunk out of a product that costs us just $1,800 (€1,600)? Aside from the thrill and fun factor, the power the Poki brings to the table has purpose: stunts .
Stunts? Yes, stunts, and ones that are controlled via hardware and software in order to assist new and experienced riders to stay in a wheelie position, one that you can even set through an app so that you can grow with the Poki as you get better at keeping your balance.
Some riders go nuts with this thing locked into a wheelie angle. Anywhere from 15 degrees to 60 degrees is on the menu here, making for some wicked Instagram videos and clips.
Photo: Jaison Bike What is neat is that we can tune acceleration, how much the brakes kick in, and much more, all with the goal of helping you tune your ride to your liking and above all, abilities. This trait of the Poki is not to be overlooked; not all minibikes out there have it.
In the range department, the Poki surprised once again, showcasing a peak range of as much as 60 miles (96.5 km) on a single charge (30 Ah battery), but best of all, in just 3 hours, it can reach an 80% charge from 20% (with fast charger), so if you stay on top of charging, you should have no worries about range.
A few other traits that need to be considered are things like wheel size, suspension, and braking, all of which are as quirky as can be, but with purpose.
Photo: Jaison Bike In the suspension department, Jaison adds a rear setup, helping control your position on the bike as you wheelie around town, but at the front, there is no softness. What helps at the front as it comes down from being in the air for however long you held the wheelie are the wheels .
The plump, 13 cm (5.1 in) wheels sit on 6-inch rims and offer ample plushness as they land, but also as you roll around city streets. Be sure to check with local laws and regulations regarding mini bike use on your streets. The tires do appear as though they could also handle some off-road use too.
Photo: Jaison Bike The smaller rubbers also help bring the center of gravity lower to the ground, so if you do happen to take a spill while you’re out there, you shouldn’t be banging yourself up too much, even less if you’re wearing proper protective gear, which, at 50 mph top speeds, you clearly should.
Honestly, after covering this little pocket beast, I can say one thing: I'll be reaching out to Jaison to see if we can get our hands on one for a test, because of you ask me, this thing is pretty neat, especially at the $1,800 we’re being asked to drop on it. Keep in mind that this is a launch price and once the sale is done, it’s set to go back to $2,600; I really hope not.
Would you ride one of these babes around town?

source_document.body:
Ministro Hales copper mine. ( Image courtesy of Codelco | Flickr. )
By: Staff Writer October 27, 2026
Workers at Codelco’s Ministro Hales copper mine in northern Chile blocked access to the operation for about six hours on Monday in a dispute over unpaid bonuses following a serious workplace accident.
Protesters erected barricades at the state-owned miner’s operation near Calama from about 6 a.m., disrupting production and access. They lifted the blockade around midday, allowing operations to begin returning to normal, the broadcaster said.
“Safety is at a standstill, and the workers are not receiving their bonuses as they should,” Alberto Muñoz, legislative director of the Federation of Copper Workers, told Cooperativa radio .
The disruption adds to labour unrest affecting major copper operations as demand for the metal grows from power grids, electric vehicles and data centres.
Safety dispute
A recent study by Santiago-based GEM Mining Consulting found that strikes, severe weather, accidents and geological problems put an average 5.2% of production at Chile’s largest copper mines at risk.
The firm’s first Production-at-Risk Index assessed 14 major copper operations across eight threats, with risk scores ranging from 2.6% to 9%. El Teniente ranked highest at 9%, followed by Los Pelambres at 8% and Escondida at 7.5%. Nine operations had at least one threat rated high.
The findings underscore the uncertainty surrounding mine production forecasts, which generally assume operations proceed as planned despite recurring disruptions from labour disputes, equipment failures and other operational challenges.
The dispute at Ministro Hales stems from a December 2025 accident in which a haul truck caught fire, leaving an operator with serious burns.
The incident forced 13 trucks and associated fleets out of service for several days, affecting bonus payments to workers. Union representatives allege that management is making employees bear the financial consequences of inadequate corporate safety practices.
Protests could spread to Codelco’s Chuquicamata, Radomiro Tomic and Gabriela Mistral operations unless senior management addresses workers’ concerns, Muñoz warned.
The possibility of further blockades raises the stakes for Codelco, whose operations are central to Chile’s copper industry. Any escalation could affect production beyond Ministro Hales.
Wider disruptions
The Chilean protest comes after more than 1,200 workers at Teck Resources’ Highland Valley Copper mine in British Columbia, Canada’s largest open-pit copper mine, walked off the job on Saturday.
The operation has continued at reduced capacity, adding another potential constraint on copper supplies.
The strike in B.C. comes as Teck pursues its merger with Anglo American (LON: AAL), a combination expected to create one of the world’s five largest copper producers.

source_document.body:
Credit: u/biggie_ballzzz on Reddit
A Rivian electric delivery van wrapped in Walmart+ branding was photographed on a car hauler on I-94 in northwest Indiana today. It’s the first public sign that Walmart could become Rivian’s next big van customer after Amazon.
Neither company has announced a deal. But Walmart’s last two electric van suppliers are out of the business, and Rivian is one of the few companies still building a purpose-built electric delivery van in the US.
A Walmart+ Rivian van on I-94
Reddit user biggie_ballzzz posted the photo to r/RIVNstock this afternoon, asking if anyone had heard about a partnership. The van is strapped to a multi-car trailer between two Ford pickups, with a big “Walmart+” logo on the side and “Same day. Right to your door.” on the rear doors.
There’s no mistaking the vehicle. It’s Rivian’s Commercial Van, with the same tall body and red light bar wrapping around the rear that you see on Amazon Prime vans everywhere.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
A few commenters suspected an AI image, but there’s no clear evidence. In fact, a second commenter then shared a photo of a van in the same livery parked in front of a Walmart Supercenter in Hammond, Indiana, about 30 miles to the west.
Rivian (RIVN) stock was up more than 3% this afternoon as the photo made the rounds, according to screenshots shared in the thread. That’s two days before Rivian reports its Q3 2026 results on Thursday, October 29.
Walmart keeps losing its electric van suppliers
Walmart has been trying to electrify last-mile delivery for years. Its supplier picks haven’t aged well.
In 2022, it signed up to buy 4,500 Canoo vans and put them to work on InHome deliveries . Canoo filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy in January 2025 and ceased operations.
The same year, Walmart reserved 5,000 BrightDrop vans from GM, and officially added them to its delivery fleet in late 2024. Then GM killed BrightDrop production at its CAMI plant in Ontario a year ago, with no plan to build the van anywhere else. BrightDrop was on pace for roughly 4,000 US sales in 2025, compared to more than 60,000 for GM’s gas-powered Express and Savana vans.
So Walmart is running two orphaned EV van platforms. And if it wants more purpose-built electric vans at scale, the list of US options is very short.
Rivian still needs a second big van customer
Amazon ordered 100,000 vans from Rivian, and its fleet has now passed 40,000 units on the road. But the deal came with an exclusivity period that ended in November 2023, and Rivian has struggled to land anything close to Amazon-scale since.
AT&T signed up for a pilot in late 2023, and HelloFresh came on board in 2025. In February 2025, Rivian opened van sales to any business , with the RCV 500 starting at $79,900 and the larger RCV 700 at $83,900. None of those customers moves the needle like Walmart would.
There’s also a charging angle. Walmart now operates its own 400 kW fast-charging network at 100 stores in 20 states , and its manager of retail charging, Wade Higgins, previously worked at Rivian, according to his bio on the board of Minnesota car-sharing nonprofit HOURCAR.
Electrek’s Take
One van on a trailer isn’t a fleet order. Not yet, anyway. This could be a test unit for a pilot program, like the one AT&T announced in 2023. And since Rivian sells vans to any business now, Walmart could have simply bought a few to try them out.
But the timing makes sense. Walmart bet on Canoo and GM, and both left it with vans nobody builds anymore. If you’re Walmart and you want to keep electrifying same-day delivery, Rivian is the obvious call. Its plant in Normal, Illinois, has already built tens of thousands of these vans, and the platform has been proven at scale by the one company Walmart is trying to beat on delivery.
That’s the awkward part. Walmart putting its brand on the same van as Amazon Prime is a bit funny, and it says a lot about how thin the electric van market has gotten in the US.
For Rivian, a Walmart deal would matter. The van business gives it volume in Normal while R2 ramps, and it badly needs proof that the van isn’t just an Amazon product. We’ll see if Rivian says anything on Thursday’s call. We wouldn’t bet on a massive order announcement, but a Walmart pilot wouldn’t surprise us one bit.

With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. 2026 SEMA Show • 2027 Dodge Charger Gets Special-Edition Package Celebrating 90 Years of Mopar
This Tiny Home Costs Just $11K, Has a Multi-Level Interior With Everything, and a Gorgeous View
20 photos
Photo: Red Cons 2000
Tiny homes come in two extremes. On one hand, we have massive and towering habitats that sit on the border of legality in terms of size, weight, and creature comforts inside, often reserved for long-term living, and on the other, we have those miniature and pint-sized habitats that squeeze as much as possible – like any tiny home should – into a space as small as possible.
Today, we’ll be exploring a conceptual tiny home from none other than Red Cons, a tiny home manufacturer from over in Romania, and whose designs stand out from others out there, even when compared to in-class options. I mean, it’s not every day that we run across something so small and well-equipped.
Photo: Red Cons 2000 Now, Red Cons is by no means a new crew, with their website mentioning that over 300 home carry their stamp of production, so clearly, this team knows precisely what it takes to build something that people want, and if I may, downright affordable.
I mean, the concept before us today, is said to cost no more than €10,000 ($11,100) to own. Sure, that doesn’t include transport, but still, that’s one hell of a price, and one that’s sure to bring an influx of potential buyers to Red Cons.
Oh, and do keep in mind that Red Cons does ship outside of Romania, so other European nations are on the menu, but it’s not clear if North America is on that list too. Considering that this team does have a shipping network in place, they just might be able to do so; give them a call if you fall in love with what you see here today and go from there.
Photo: Red Cons 2000 What you do need to keep in mind is that if you do bring one over to the US, you’ll need to make adjustments to the electrical system, if Red Cons doesn’t build to 110-120V standards. Maybe leave the electrical out and do it yourself once you have it sitting on that reserved lot of yours.
Which brings me to my next point: this concept does not have any sort of wheels underneath, so you will need a foundation for it, albeit not a very large one. Just under 3 m (9.8 ft) is the length of each of sides. At its highest point – it does have a sloping roof – the habitat sits at around 3.8 m (12.5 ft) without any stilts.
Since space is extremely limited on each plane, Red Cons decided to build on a verticle plane, with the lower level reserved for a daily lounge, bathroom, and fully stocked kitchen, and the upper level for the bedroom. The two spaces are connected via a staircase that sits right by the entrance to the home .
Photo: Red Cons 2000 While details are limited as to what we can find inside this habitat in terms of systems, some things are obvious, and one of them is the induction cooktop, an object that leads me to believe that either there’s an off-grid-ready system in place here or that shore power is to be called upon. Both are valid solutions.
The rest of the kitchen is completed with a storage above and below, a convection oven, gorgeous warm LED light provided by strips, and a floor to ceiling window that lets you cook with a view.
Across from the kitchen and separated by a wall of particle board or unlaminated MDF, is the bathroom, a space which, if I may, would be a downright pleasure to use. Not only is there ample space inside, but residential features are showcased, which are sure to cost extra and probably don’t fall into the price that Red Cons mentioned. If they do, ooo-weee!
Photo: Red Cons 2000 As mentioned, to access the upper level, there's a staircase by the entrance to the home, and if we follow its steps, we’ll be led to a loft bedroom that has walls completed from glass in order to grant us a view of the world outside right from bed. Just picture the sunrises ; Instagram-worthy all day!
Another trait of this tiny home concept that I wish to bring to light is the presence of all the particle board inside this thing. Sure, this material is primarily used inside as the interior paneling, but some folks are sure to feel like it’s a bit cheap. Keep in mind that some proper paint can cover up that look.
The exterior, on the other hand, is one that sees a different kind of treatment, with what appears to be pine, a readily available wood in the region. Toss on a metal roof, some metallic and darkened accents here and there, a couple of spotlights, and we have ourselves a tiny home that doesn’t just look attractive, but is, in every sense of the word, especially price.
Photo: Red Cons 2000 Eleven hundred dollars is a sweet deal, even with the extra bucks we need to drop on features and systems if they aren’t included in that price.
Red Cons also to the time to picture a tourist or worksite that places this concept in the center of its action, and if I may, what I'm seeing looks pretty good, and isn’t the most expensive investment out there if you’re looking to start a B&B.
